items.title: Suppressing neural stem cell PLA2G7 restores inhibitory circuit function and improves cognition in aging mice
items.author: Nannan Guo
items.content: Wu, Wu and colleagues identify PLA2G7, a secreted lipid-metabolizing enzyme, as a negative regulator of inhibitory synapses in the dentate gyrus. Suppression of PLA2G7 in neural stem cells enhances synaptic transmission and cognitive performance in aged mice.

items.title: Transcriptomic reprogramming screen identifies SRSF1 as a regulator of aging
items.author: George M. Church
items.content: Plesa, Jung and colleagues conduct an in vitro transcriptomic reprogramming screen and identify splicing factor SRSF1 as capable of reducing transcriptomic age without loss of cell identity; they then implicate SRSF1 as a regulator of aging in worms and mice.

items.title: Senescent-like activated naive B cells contribute to progression to clinical rheumatoid arthritis
items.author: William H. Robinson
items.content: Applying single-cell multiomics to people at risk of rheumatoid arthritis, Wu, Zhang, Moon and colleagues identify an expansion of activated, senescent-like B cells associated with disease development. These cells express poly- and autoreactive antibodies and present self-antigens to T cells.

items.title: Brain DNA methylation, APOE genotype and Alzheimer’s disease neuropathology in a large postmortem cohort
items.author: Jinying Zhao
items.content: A large-scale study identified 107 brain DNA methylation sites linked to Alzheimer’s pathology, with 38 replicated independently. DNA methylation partially mediated the association between APOE genotype and Alzheimer’s diagnosis.

items.title: Lymph node contraction links sex-biased naive CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell decline to compromised antigen recognition during middle age
items.author: Timothy P. Padera
items.content: Menzel and colleagues report that male mice and humans undergo accelerated immune aging, characterized by naive CD8+ T cell decline and early thymic involution, which impairs cancer antigen recognition and response to immunotherapy.

items.title: Naive T cell decline limits cancer immunity in middle-aged male mice
items.content: Using mice and supporting human data, we show that accelerated loss of naive CD8+ T cells in male mice leads to lymph node contraction and limited cancer antigen recognition. Restoring thymic output replenished naive CD8+ T cells and improved responses to immunotherapy in middle-aged male mice.

items.title: Heterogeneity in secondary follicle development buffers the lifespan of activated oocytes to optimize female fertility in mice
items.author: Hua Zhang
items.content: Liang, Yang and colleagues map the developmental dynamics of activated oocytes and folliculogenesis across the reproductive lifespan using lineage tracing in mice. Their work reveals marked heterogeneity in the lifespan of activated oocytes in growing follicles, which form a secondary ovarian reserve that buffers oocyte utilization and sustains fertility.
